title: Training method for cluster vehicle cooperative learning
assignee: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

pse.problem: Existing CVFL methods have limitations in accurately clustering vehicle clients and encouraging multiple clusters to train federated learning tasks simultaneously.
pse.solution_function: The invention presents a method for cooperative learning of cluster vehicles that uses an iterative K-means algorithm to group and aggregate local models of vehicle clients obtained from the server's broadcasted global model, performs accurate clustering of the local model by cluster head selection, cluster head matching model, and vehicle client matching cluster head, utilizes a two-layer incentive mechanism for motivating both cluster heads and vehicle clients, and sends optimal contracts and global model information within the cluster to each vehicle client for local training.
pse.solution_structure: The system consists of server, cluster heads, and vehicle clients. The server broadcasts and aggregates global models, cluster heads perform accurate clustering and contract formation, and vehicle clients perform local training and data uploading.
pse.solution_implementation: In the first step, the server broadcasts the global model to vehicle clients within its coverage area, receives local models from each vehicle client, and aggregates them using the K-means algorithm. In the second step, the vehicle client performs accurate clustering through cluster head selection, matching of cluster head model, and matching with a cluster head. In the third step, a two-layer incentive mechanism is used: an upper layer incentivizes each cluster head using a master-slave game mechanism, and a lower layer encourages vehicle clients in the cluster using a multi-dimensional contract theory mechanism. In the fourth step, the cluster head sends the optimal contract and global model information within the cluster to each vehicle client for local training.
pse.effect: The solution results in accurate clustering of vehicle clients and simultaneous training of multiple federated learning tasks, improving training efficiency.
